x: The 'loss' of Bill and Roger has been compensated for by the acquisition of two Antipodeans, Kelly Diprose and Bob Smith. Kelly is a Kiwi and Bob a Kangaroo (or is it a Wallaby?).

We already knew about Kelly Diprose, having seen him in action in the North Surrey League and in the Dudley to Bridgenorth relay earlier, but we knew little or nothing about Bob Smith who is in this country for a time as a dentist in Croydon.

A few weeks ago we had visions of a strong enough team to win this race but with the departure of Roger Donnison for a job in Exeter, the sickness over Christmas and the New Year of Kelly Diprose and the injury of Bob Smith we were deprived of three potential scorers.
Our new 10,000 metres champion, Bob Smith, is now back to his form of 10 months ago and there is every prospect of his turning in some fast times.

Geoff North's brilliant Southern run was the obvious highlight, but at National League and Trphy level, we were generally under-represented. It was encouraging, however, to welcome Gerry North and Bob Smith back to fitness by the end of the season.

Forty-two Belgravians toed the line and ten finished in the first 34 of the 140 finishers to clinch a win that certainly shook our opponents. Lionel Mann and Bob Smith were in great form to lead our team home with Doug Brew also showing up well to close in our scorers.

His main rival over here, though they rarely clashed, was Bob Smith. It is Belgrave's good fortune that Aussie Bob has decided to settle in England---and to prove the point he recently got married and bought a house in Purley!.
Bob Smith, now permanently resident and in practice as a dentist in Croydon, has just returned after a 3 months spell in his native Australia.

After the first lap of the common it was Trevor Hart in the 'drivers seat' with a neat bunch of about 8 gathered around him including a bronzed Bob Smith, recently back from Australia and the most recent addition to our ranks Guy Monnet who hails from France.
One of the most pleasing performances was by Bob Smith who not only made his debut at road relay running but at road racing as well. So Belgrave had "come right" at last, but was it too early?
Bob Smith and John Bicourt lead the chase after Bob Holt (H/W) in the Surrey County 5,000m Championships at Motspur Park. Holt (14:14.6) won from Bob (14:23.6) with John taking the bronze in 14:39.8.

Whilst on the subject of valuable club men we surely have another in Bob Smith. Not just for his performances for,as reported elsewhere,this season has been his first outing on the road for us; but for his club spirit and enthusiasm which put some longer serving members to shame.
Other promising runs have come from Peter Carton, Bill Curtin, Bill Kerr, Adrian Major, Bob Smith and Jim Rimmer. This could be one of our stronger events.

The defending champion, Bob Smith, was down with injury but brought the Cup along and stayed to see who would next be polishing it. Nineteen runners fought for the privilege, but after 1200metres only six were in contention.
Laurie O'Hara looks in good nick, while Bob Smith has the ability to lift the team several degrees, if he has the application, and Alan Black has been showing promising form.

Bob Smith produced some promising form, touring the five-mile course in splendid isolation for a 29m. 31s clocking. Gerry North gave the field a two-minute start, and just edged into second place, ahead of Tony Fairclough, while Alan Black held off the challenge of Brian Gorman, to take fourth place.
His performance in beating men like Trevor Hart, Alan Black and Pat O'Connor, as well as Bob Smith and Tony Fairclough, gave him a well deserved win in the handicap.

It was good to see Bob Smith (309th) out in the National, however, while Tony Fairclough plugged away as grittily as ever, and we congratulate Colin Pearson on his first appearance in the National scoring six.

Fortunately, Bob Smith and Jim Rimmer are going very well and Trevor Hart should repeat his 20th place of last year. Leading us home, we hope, will be Gerry North with his regular place inside the first ten.

Laurie gave his all, around the roads he knows so well from past '5¾'victories, fighting for every second that he could give to our anchor man Bob Smith.
Stage four was taken by Bob Smith, who despite giving his best, lost ground to Whitty of T.V.H. although he managed to overtake Beard of Hercules Wimbledon.
Both Lionel and Gerry North looked fitter than of late, and, gaining a first class standard, Bob Smith made a most welcome return to the Belgrave scene.

The only flaw in Laurie's astounding record is the fact that he has not as yet gained the championship best time, his fastest in this race being 30:57.6 in '72 compared to Bob Smith's 30:31.2 in 1969 when the race first went metric.

Pat O'Connor had the measure of Bill Weller on this occasion and it was good to see Bob Smith scoring for us again. Peter Gardner crept ever nearer the scorers being our 11th man and only 7 seconds down on Lionel Mann.

…rtably our first man but there was a rare old tussle to fill the last scoring place, with Alan Black just losing out to Bob Smith It was interesting to note that the six clubs ahead of us in the team race were all from division one of the Surrey League with the 7th member of that league, Herne Hill…

Also notable were Tony Binda's return to form, Bob Smith's business like return to the road running scene as well as our younger stars, Mark Waller and Mark Sinclair making their presence felt in senior company with first class times for their ages.

Bob Smith and Tony Fairclough have also bounced back with a vengeance to show that they are by no means 'over the hill' and John Bicourt hopefully now free from injury has had a better season for us than for quite a while.
Bob Smith had steadily been getting the track pace back in his legs and a week after his 9:01.3 3 km at Tooting, he put his name on the 'Tom Carter' Cup once more.

It is ironic that fate should choose this race for people like Ian Duncan, Pat O'Connor and Bob Smith, some of the seasons most consistent and reliable performers, to have a bad one.

We must not forget another "Aussie", Cross-country, Road and Track runner, Bob Smith. We are now up to those currently performing, they figure in our teams and we are proud of them, but two names stand out and must be included.
